runDescription: 100 seeds x 10,000 requests (Extended Baseline and Robustness Final Evaluation)

experimentSize.note: Same workload used for all 5 policies per seed. Policy-level evaluations are NOT independent observations.

adaptive_piper_count_identity.identity: finalPiperCount == directHardFailureFallbacks + circuitBreakerFallbacks (100% match across all 600 Adaptive seeds)

qmin_does_not_affect_routing.note: Q_min changes QVR classification only. Routing decisions, success rate, cost, and piper usage unaffected.

same_workload_all_policies.note: Workload hash matches identically across all 5 policies for each seed.

scientificLanguageCommitments.cloudPenaltyMsNote: cloudPenaltyMs (500/1000/2000ms) is an assumption in Sensitivity Analysis, NOT a measured timeout from real system traces.
scientificLanguageCommitments.qMinNote: Q_min changes QVR classification and calculation only. Routing decisions and provider selection are unaffected.
scientificLanguageCommitments.circuitBreakerStatement: The circuit-breaker policy reduced repeated failed calls to an unavailable cloud dependency under the evaluated simulated conditions.
tradeoffSummary: 1. CloudWithPerRequestFallback retained slightly higher conditional quality, whereas Adaptive reduced failed cloud attempts during the simulated 60-second outage, at the cost of slightly greater local fallback usage and quality-threshold violations.
2. Circuit Breaker reduces repeated failed calls to the cloud dependency and may reduce cost during outages.
3. When Piper fails (piperFailRate > 0), SuccessRate falls below 100%; results are evaluated as Robustness Sensitivity, not an Availability guarantee.
